title: ～てみる — “try ～ing”
summary: Add みる to the te-form to mean doing something to see what happens, or trying. It is used for deliberate actions.

patterns.gloss: Verb te-form + みる (食べてみる)
～てみてもいいですか (May I try ～?)

body.p: For food, clothes, new methods, or anything where you want to see how it turns out. Also common when asking: 試着してみる, 聞いてみる.
It cannot be used for events that happen by themselves or unconscious actions (× 雨が降ってみる). As an auxiliary, みる is normally written in kana.

examples.ja: 新（あたら）しいレストランで食（た）べてみます。
examples.tr: I'll try eating at the new restaurant.

examples.ja: この赤（あか）いくつをはいてみてもいいですか。
examples.romaji: Kono akai kutsu o haite mite mo ii desu ka.
examples.tr: May I try on these red shoes?

examples.ja: 難（むずか）しそうだけど、一度（いちど）自分（じぶん）で作（つく）ってみます。
examples.romaji: Muzukashisō da kedo, ichido jibun de tsukutte mimasu.
examples.tr: It looks hard, but I'll try making it myself once.

pitfalls: Not for natural events or involuntary actions.
Write it in kana (みる), not the kanji 見る.
